newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST - Hydro Q1 profits seen falling.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Hydro Q1 profits seen falling.

text.p: Norwegian industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA is expected to post 1997 first-quarter pre-tax profits of about 2.86 billion crowns, down from 3.33 billion in the same year-ago period, according to 10 analysts polled by Reuters.

Three analysts downgraded their recommendations from before Hydro presented its annual 1996 result although the share has dropped more than 14 percent since then. The share closed at 325.50 crowns on the Oslo Bourse on Monday.
Five analysts said hold, two said buy while one who previously said buy now suggested to sell Hydro stock. The remaining two analysts declined to give a recommendation.
Hydro's agriculture division was the focus of most uncertainty with forecasts varying widely.
Optimistic analysts believed volume would increase compared to 1996 and that a price fall on Hydro fertilizers was much lower than the market generally thinks.
The pessimists saw a bad start of the year with reduced volume and miserable prices.
But most analysts were positive to agriculture in the long term.

Hydro's plans to expand in agriculture and light metals in the next few years generally received a blessing. But it also prompted speculation Hydro might sell some non-core business, such as its long-time shareholding in Dyno Industrier ASA.
Analysts by and large saw a long-term positive price development for petrochemicals and light metals, including aluminium.
Hydro, which is 50 percent owned by the Norwegian government, will present the first-quarter result on April 21.
